This is the code in question that is erroring:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/50277787eacaf4bc4d8683a706fe54dc65762020/platform/android/jni_utils.cpp#L422-L442

Seems to treat this argument incorrectly (not sure if it is supposed to support `java.util.HashMap`, or if the method name is incorrect in that case)

Seems like it was never supposed to support HashMaps and it only checks for HashMaps because Dictionary class extends this.

cc @godotengine/android

We should just deprecate Godot `Dictionary` and update the logic to use the `HashMap` api instead. Now that we have `javaclasswrapper`, it's no longer useful.

@syntaxerror247 Can you prepare a fix for it.

I got the same crash in 4.5.1.

> We should just deprecate Godot `Dictionary` and update the logic to use the `HashMap` api instead. Now that we have `javaclasswrapper`, it's no longer useful.

~Agree, but~ I think a java map or collection (e.g. lists) should continue to be accessible as a `JavaObject` from GDScript.
But java arrays of objects (i.e. not packed arrays) should be accessible as a godot `Array`, maybe `Array[JavaObject]` (if we're not worried about things like nested arrays, etc). Or keep it as `JavaObject`, but fix it so calling indexers like `array[i]` works from GDScript (they currently don't work if I'm not mistaken).

hmm.. my thoughts were to turn instances of java map into a Godot `Dictionary` on the gdscript side, and convert it back to a map when passing back to the java side to leverage built-in gdscript component as much as possible. Similar to how we turn a java String into a gdscript String instead of keeping it as a JavaObject.

> Similar to how we turn a java String into a gdscript String instead of keeping it as a JavaObject.

@m4gr3d You're missing a key difference though.

With java `String` and `T[]`/`Array`, they're `final` classes within the `java.lang` package. They cannot be extended and `String` is even immutable -- they're as close as you get to primitive types. Their behavior is stable and predictable.

With `java.util` collections and maps such as `ArrayList` and `HashMap`, however, it's a very different story -- these are specific utility classes that can even be extended, methods overriden, etc.
Let's say you gotta deal with some lib's class that defines a `veryImportantMethod()` you need to call from GDScript, but that class just so happens to extend `HashMap`, now what do you do if it's automatically turned into a godot `Dictionary`?

So, on second thought I actually disagree now, I'm against deprecating `Dictionary`. It was added for a reason (unlike `Array`, there's no "primitive" equivalent in java) and we should leave java classes alone. Here's my suggestions:
1. We should fix this issue by just converting only godot `Dictionary` as intended and not every `HashMap`. Don't deprecate it, because `HashMap` is a different thing, so it's not useless. Better to leave the concepts separate and avoid problems.
2. In fact, if we're changing things, we should fix the java wrapper `Dictionary` class to be `final` (since it's a godot basic type) and extend from `HashMap<Object, Object>`, since godot does not require dictionary keys to be strings; any godot object can be a key. I guess that's a breaking change, so it can be 4.7+ stuff.
3. Convert `T[]` into a godot `Array` (can be untyped), taking care to recursively convert its element types as needed e.g. `MyClass[] <-> Array[JavaObject]`, `MyClass[][] -> Array[Array]`, `long[][] <-> Array[PackedInt64Array]`, etc.
  Either that or implement an indexer operator into `JavaObject` just for arrays, or make a new `JavaArray` class, if that's feasible. This way we can call indexers from GDScript and use arrays as intended.
  I didn't look if there's already any proposal in this regard.

> * We should fix this issue by just converting only godot `Dictionary` as intended and not every `HashMap`. Don't deprecate it, because `HashMap` is a different thing, so it's not useless. Better to leave the concepts separate and avoid problems.
> * In fact, if we're changing things, we should fix the java wrapper `Dictionary` class to be `final` (since it's a godot basic type) and extend from `HashMap<Object, Object>`, since godot does not require dictionary keys to be strings; any godot object can be a key. I guess that's a breaking change, so it can be 4.7+ stuff.

We should proceed with deprecating [`org.godotengine.godot.Dictionary`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.6/platform/android/java/lib/src/main/java/org/godotengine/godot/Dictionary.java) as the current implementation provides no benefits and no custom functionality over a regular `HashMap`, and proceed with the initial proposal, **but only restrict conversion to Godot Dictionary for only `java.util.HashMap`**. All other `Map` types or classes derived from `java.util.HashMap` will be wrapped by a `JavaObject`. This would map the current behavior and prevent breaking backward compat.

> Convert T[] into a godot Array (can be untyped), taking care to recursively convert its element types as needed e.g. MyClass[] <-> Array[JavaObject], MyClass[][] -> Array[Array], long[][] <-> Array[PackedInt64Array], etc.
Either that or implement an indexer operator into JavaObject just for arrays, or make a new JavaArray class, if that's feasible. This way we can call indexers from GDScript and use arrays as intended.
I didn't look if there's already any proposal in this regard.

@geekley Java arrays should already be converted to the equivalent Godot arrays; is that not working for you?

> We should proceed with deprecating [org.godotengine.godot.Dictionary](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.6/platform/android/java/lib/src/main/java/org/godotengine/godot/Dictionary.java) as the current implementation provides no benefits and no custom functionality over a regular HashMap, and proceed with the initial proposal, but only restrict conversion to Godot Dictionary for only java.util.HashMap. All other Map types or classes derived from java.util.HashMap will be wrapped by a JavaObject. This would map the current behavior and prevent breaking backward compat.

@m4gr3d I dunno about that. What if I expect to deal with a java hashmap in GDScript for whatever reason? For example to pass to a java method/callback/etc that needs a hashmap parameter? Will it be correctly converted back and forth everywhere, including nested objects, and in JavaClassWrapper, plugins `@UsedByGodot` and signals?
If so that's OK, but I dunno how nested conversions work, it seems very unreliable.
In fact I've had an issue where I got, IIRC, from a signal sent from java plugin to godot with a TreeMap parameter, a map entry from GDScript (I was iterating) and instead of a GDScript string, I somehow (I think getting key from the entry) got a java String as JavaObject so when I did `str(key)` it did the `"JavaObject<java.lang.String "etc">"` or whatever the format is -- i.e. it added stuff to the string instead of just `"etc"`.

@geekley @m4gr3d I've updated the PR.

Now it doesn't deprecate `org.godotengine.godot.Dictionary`, and HashMap is returned as a JavaObject.
